nodes.title: SG-7.9 Coding agent provider with a labelled mock, chosen by provider kind
nodes.body:
Context: the worker runner (backend/worker/internal/runner/runner.go) defines the Agent interface, and config already validates provider_kind as mock or claude. No implementation of Agent exists. Desired behavior: a provider package supplies a mock agent that says it is a mock, a Claude CLI adapter, and a factory that picks one from provider_kind. Expected result: the runner can be built with an Agent chosen from config. Why: mock runs must never be mistaken for real development.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given provider_kind is mock, When the factory is called, Then it returns the mock agent, which satisfies runner.Agent
- Given the mock agent runs, When it finishes, Then the work dir holds a file that states it is a MOCK run and the cost is 0
- Given provider_kind is claude, When the factory is called, Then it returns the Claude adapter
- Given an unknown provider_kind, When the factory is called, Then it returns an error naming the kind


## Scope
- In scope: new package backend/worker/internal/provider
- In scope: mock agent
- In scope: Claude CLI adapter behind an Exec interface
- In scope: factory keyed by provider kind
- Out of scope: changes to the runner retry logic
- Out of scope: real Claude invocation in tests
- Out of scope: analysis, requirements and task generation
- Preserve: runner.Agent signature
- Preserve: config validation of provider_kind


## Technical constraints
- Go module github.com/worldseed/storyforge/worker at backend/worker
- Never interpolate player text into a shell
- The agent is passed arguments as a slice, not a shell string


## Definition of done
- All requirements are met and their Verify units pass


## Non-functional requirements
- Mock output must be unmistakably labelled


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Mock provider runs as a runner.Agent and labels its output as mock
nodes.body:
Context: no Agent implementation exists. Desired behavior: Mock.Run(ctx, workDir) writes MOCK-EXECUTION.md saying no real development happened and returns cost 0. Expected result: mock runs are distinguishable from real ones. Why: the master prompt requires mock execution to be clearly distinguished.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a temp work dir, When Mock.Run is called, Then MOCK-EXECUTION.md exists and contains the text MOCK
- Given Mock.Run succeeds, When the cost is read, Then it equals 0 and the error is nil
- Given a cancelled context, When Mock.Run is called, Then it returns the context error and writes no file


## Scope
- In scope: Mock type and Run
- In scope: Mock.Name returning mock
- Out of scope: editing game source
- Preserve: runner.Agent signature


## Technical constraints
- Write only inside workDir


## Definition of done
- Mock satisfies runner.Agent


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Claude adapter runs the CLI through an Exec interface with a fixed argument list
nodes.body:
Context: provider_kind claude is accepted by config but has no agent. Desired behavior: Claude.Run calls Exec.Run(ctx, workDir, "claude", args) with args built from a constant prompt telling it to implement the structured tasks, never player text, and returns cost 0 or the wrapped error. Expected result: a real adapter that tests can fake. Why: community prompts are untrusted.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a fake Exec, When Claude.Run is called with workDir W, Then Exec receives dir W, name claude and a non-empty args slice
- Given Exec returns an error, When Claude.Run is called, Then the error is returned wrapped with provider claude
- Given a nil Exec, When NewClaude is called, Then it returns an error


## Scope
- In scope: Exec interface
- In scope: Claude type, NewClaude, Run
- Out of scope: a real os/exec implementation of Exec
- Out of scope: parsing agent cost
- Preserve: runner.Agent signature


## Technical constraints
- No sh -c
- Prompt is a package constant


## Definition of done
- Claude satisfies runner.Agent


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Factory selects the agent from the configured provider kind
nodes.body:
Context: config.Worker.ProviderKind holds mock or claude. Desired behavior: provider.New(kind, exec) returns the Mock for mock, the Claude adapter for claude and an error for any other value. Expected result: the runner can be built from config. Why: selection must be driven by config.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given kind mock, When New is called, Then the result is a Mock
- Given kind claude and a fake Exec, When New is called, Then the result is a Claude
- Given kind gpt, When New is called, Then the error text contains gpt
- Given kind claude and a nil Exec, When New is called, Then it returns an error


## Scope
- In scope: New factory
- Out of scope: editing cmd wiring, which does not exist yet
- Preserve: config constants


## Technical constraints
- Kind strings match config: mock and claude


## Dependencies
- R1
- R2


## Definition of done
- Factory covers both kinds

- None

steps.action: Create package provider with type Mock struct{}, const MockMarkerFile = "MOCK-EXECUTION.md", method Name() string returning "mock" and method Run(ctx context.Context, workDir string) (float64, error). Run returns ctx.Err() when it is already non-nil, otherwise writes MockMarkerFile in workDir with os.WriteFile mode 0o644 and returns 0 and nil, wrapping a write failure as provider mock.

This run used the MOCK provider. No real development happened.
"
steps.expected: go build ./internal/provider succeeds and the file is written on Run
